title: 1 Kings Chapter 22 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Kings chapter 22 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Kings Chapter 22 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Kings Chapter 22.

questions.question: How many years did Syria and Israel continue without war?
questions.correctAnswer: Three years
questions.explanation: The text states that they continued three years without war between Syria and Israel (1 Kings 22:1).

questions.question: Who came down to the king of Israel in the third year?
questions.correctAnswer: Jehoshaphat the king of Judah
questions.explanation: In the third year, Jehoshaphat the king of Judah came down to the king of Israel (1 Kings 22:2).

questions.question: What city did the king of Israel say was theirs but still held by the king of Syria?
questions.correctAnswer: Ramoth in Gilead
questions.explanation: The king of Israel said Ramoth in Gilead is theirs, but they have not taken it from the king of Syria (1 Kings 22:3).

questions.question: What was Jehoshaphat's response when asked to go to battle with the king of Israel?
options: I am as thou art, my people as thy people, my horses as thy horses
I will send my army instead
I need to consult the prophets first
questions.correctAnswer: I am as thou art, my people as thy people, my horses as thy horses
questions.explanation: Jehoshaphat said, 'I am as thou art, my people as thy people, my horses as thy horses' (1 Kings 22:4).

questions.question: What did Jehoshaphat ask the king of Israel to do before going to battle?
options: Enquire at the word of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Enquire at the word of the LORD
questions.explanation: Jehoshaphat said, 'Enquire, I pray thee, at the word of the LORD to day' (1 Kings 22:5).

questions.question: How many prophets did the king of Israel gather to inquire about the battle?
questions.correctAnswer: About 400
questions.explanation: The king of Israel gathered about four hundred prophets (1 Kings 22:6).

questions.question: What advice did the four hundred prophets give about going to Ramothgilead?
options: Go up; for the Lord shall deliver it into the hand of the king
questions.correctAnswer: Go up; for the Lord shall deliver it into the hand of the king
questions.explanation: They said, 'Go up; for the Lord shall deliver it into the hand of the king' (1 Kings 22:6).

questions.question: Who was the prophet that the king of Israel hated because he prophesied evil against him?
questions.correctAnswer: Micaiah the son of Imlah
questions.explanation: The king said he hated Micaiah because he did not prophesy good concerning him, but evil (1 Kings 22:8).

questions.question: Where did the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat sit when hearing the prophets?
options: On their thrones in the entrance of the gate of Samaria
questions.correctAnswer: On their thrones in the entrance of the gate of Samaria
questions.explanation: They sat each on his throne at the entrance of the gate of Samaria (1 Kings 22:10).

questions.question: What did Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah make to symbolize the LORD's command?
questions.correctAnswer: Horns of iron
questions.explanation: Zedekiah made horns of iron and said, 'With these shalt thou push the Syrians' (1 Kings 22:11).

questions.question: True or False: Micaiah agreed to speak only what was good to the king when called.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Micaiah said he would speak what the LORD saith, not only what is good (1 Kings 22:14).

questions.question: True or False: Micaiah prophesied that the LORD would deliver Ramothgilead into the king's hand.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Micaiah actually prophesied that Israel would be scattered and have no master (1 Kings 22:17).

questions.question: True or False: Jehoshaphat asked if there was another prophet of the LORD to inquire of besides the four hundred.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jehoshaphat asked if there was another prophet of the LORD to inquire of (1 Kings 22:7).

questions.question: True or False: The king of Israel immediately accepted Micaiah's prophecy without suspicion.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The king expressed suspicion and anger, saying Micaiah prophesied evil and adjured him to tell the truth (1 Kings 22:16, 18).

questions.question: In the order of events, which came first in 1 Kings 22:1-18?
options: Jehoshaphat asks to enquire of the LORD
The king gathers four hundred prophets
Jehoshaphat visits the king of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Jehoshaphat visits the king of Israel
questions.explanation: Jehoshaphat visiting the king occurs first (verse 2), then the king gathers prophets (6), Jehoshaphat asks to enquire of the LORD (5), and finally Micaiah is called (9).

medium.title: 1 Kings Chapter 22 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Kings Chapter 22 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What vision did Micaiah describe to King Ahab concerning Israel's fate?
options: Israel will triumph over Syria and gain Ramothgilead
Israel will be scattered like sheep without a shepherd
Israel will form an alliance with Judah and prosper
Israel will conquer all its enemies quickly
questions.correctAnswer: Israel will be scattered like sheep without a shepherd
questions.explanation: Micaiah told Ahab that he saw Israel scattered upon the hills like sheep without a shepherd, meaning they would have no leader and return home in peace (1 Kings 22:17). This vision contrasts the false prophets' message and is affirmed in 1 Kings 22:19-20 where the LORD discusses Ahab's downfall.

questions.question: According to 1 Kings 22:19-23, why did the LORD put a lying spirit in the mouths of Ahab's prophets?
options: To persuade Ahab to go into battle and fall
To warn Ahab to avoid the battle
To encourage Jehoshaphat to lead the battle
questions.correctAnswer: To persuade Ahab to go into battle and fall
questions.explanation: The LORD allowed a spirit to be a lying spirit in the mouths of Ahab's prophets to persuade Ahab to go to Ramothgilead where he would fall, as the LORD had decreed (1 Kings 22:20-23). This shows God's sovereignty even over deception to fulfill His purposes.

questions.question: How does the passage in 1 Kings 22:24-25 illustrate the consequences of opposing God's true prophet?
options: Zedekiah was rewarded for opposing Micaiah
Zedekiah was struck by Micaiah's prophecy of hiding in fear
Zedekiah was promoted to a higher position
questions.correctAnswer: Zedekiah was struck by Micaiah's prophecy of hiding in fear
questions.explanation: Zedekiah struck Micaiah on the cheek for speaking against him, but Micaiah prophesied that Zedekiah would hide in an inner chamber on the day of the battle, indicating divine judgment on those who oppose God's message (1 Kings 22:24-25).

questions.question: What instructions did Ahab give concerning Micaiah after his unfavorable prophecy?
options: Set him free and honor him
Put him in prison and feed him with bread and water of affliction
Send him on a diplomatic mission to Syria
Make him chief prophet of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Put him in prison and feed him with bread and water of affliction
questions.explanation: Ahab ordered Micaiah to be taken to prison and fed with bread and water of affliction until the king returned in peace, showing how leaders sometimes reject and punish God's true messengers (1 Kings 22:26-27).

questions.question: What warning did Micaiah give about Ahab's return from battle?
options: Ahab will return victorious and safe
If Ahab returns at all in peace, the LORD has not spoken by Micaiah
Ahab will be captured by the Syrians
Ahab will become king of Syria
questions.correctAnswer: If Ahab returns at all in peace, the LORD has not spoken by Micaiah
questions.explanation: Micaiah declared that if Ahab returned safely, it would mean the LORD had not spoken through him, emphasizing the certainty of Ahab's downfall as a consequence of disobedience (1 Kings 22:28).

questions.question: Why did King Ahab disguise himself before entering the battle at Ramothgilead?
options: To avoid being recognized by Jehoshaphat
Because he was ashamed to fight openly
To protect himself from being targeted by enemies
To deceive the king of Syria
questions.correctAnswer: To protect himself from being targeted by enemies
questions.explanation: Ahab disguised himself to avoid being singled out as the king of Israel in battle, as the king of Syria had specifically instructed his captains to fight only the king of Israel (1 Kings 22:30-31).

questions.question: What mistake did the Syrian captains make during the battle regarding Jehoshaphat?
options: They mistook Jehoshaphat for the king of Israel and attacked him
They allied with Jehoshaphat against Ahab
questions.correctAnswer: They mistook Jehoshaphat for the king of Israel and attacked him
questions.explanation: The Syrian captains saw Jehoshaphat wearing royal robes and assumed he was the king of Israel, so they turned to fight him, causing Jehoshaphat to cry out, but they ceased pursuit when they realized their error (1 Kings 22:32-33).

questions.question: How was King Ahab fatally wounded in the battle?
options: He was struck by a spear thrown by a Syrian captain
He was shot between the joints of his armor by a man shooting at random
He fell from his chariot and broke his neck
He was struck down by Jehoshaphat's men
questions.correctAnswer: He was shot between the joints of his armor by a man shooting at random
questions.explanation: A certain man drew a bow at random and struck Ahab between the joints of his armor, causing a mortal wound that led to his death that evening (1 Kings 22:34-35).

questions.question: What proclamation was made throughout the army at sunset after the battle?
options: Prepare for a second assault at dawn
Every man return to his city and country
Celebrate the victory over the Syrians
Capture the prisoners and loot the camp
questions.correctAnswer: Every man return to his city and country
questions.explanation: At sunset, a proclamation was made for every man to return to his city and own country, signaling the end of the battle and the cessation of fighting (1 Kings 22:36).

questions.question: What does 1 Kings 22:19-23 teach us about God's sovereignty over events, even involving deception?
options: God allows deception to fulfill His righteous purposes
God is unaware of human actions and plans
questions.correctAnswer: God allows deception to fulfill His righteous purposes
questions.explanation: The passage shows that God orchestrated the lying spirit to deceive Ahab's prophets so that Ahab would be persuaded to his downfall, demonstrating God's ultimate control over all events (1 Kings 22:19-23).

questions.question: How does the interaction between Ahab and Micaiah demonstrate the importance of truth in leadership?
options: Ahab welcomed all prophecies regardless of content
Ahab rejected Micaiah’s truthful prophecy because it was unfavorable
Micaiah only prophesied what Ahab wanted to hear
Micaiah’s prophecy was ignored because it was too positive
questions.correctAnswer: Ahab rejected Micaiah’s truthful prophecy because it was unfavorable
questions.explanation: Ahab admitted he hated Micaiah because he did not prophesy good concerning him but evil, showing how leaders may reject truth when it conflicts with their desires (1 Kings 22:8, 18).

questions.question: True or False: Jehoshaphat agreed with Ahab’s plan to attack Ramothgilead without seeking the LORD’s guidance.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jehoshaphat insisted on enquiring of the LORD before going to battle, showing the importance of seeking God’s guidance in decisions (1 Kings 22:5).

questions.question: True or False: The LORD’s judgment against Ahab was fulfilled as Micaiah predicted, resulting in Ahab’s death in battle.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Micaiah prophesied that Ahab would fall at Ramothgilead, and Ahab was fatally wounded and died that day, fulfilling the LORD’s judgment (1 Kings 22:35, 28).

questions.question: True or False: Jehoshaphat wore disguise in the battle to avoid being targeted like Ahab.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: It was Ahab who disguised himself, while Jehoshaphat wore his royal robes, which led the Syrian captains to mistake him for Ahab (1 Kings 22:30-32).

questions.question: According to 1 Kings 22:25 and 1 Kings 22:33, what practical lesson can believers learn about facing adversity and deception?
options: Opponents of God’s truth often face unexpected consequences
questions.correctAnswer: Opponents of God’s truth often face unexpected consequences
questions.explanation: Zedekiah opposed Micaiah and was told he would hide in fear, while the Syrians were deceived in battle and ceased pursuit when realizing the truth, illustrating how opposing God’s truth results in consequences (1 Kings 22:25, 33).

hard.title: 1 Kings Chapter 22 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Kings Chapter 22.

questions.question: According to 1 Kings 22, where was King Ahab buried after his death?
questions.correctAnswer: In Samaria
questions.explanation: Verse 37 states that Ahab died and was brought to Samaria where he was buried.

questions.question: What unusual event involving animals happened at Ahab's chariot as described in 1 Kings 22?
questions.correctAnswer: Dogs licked up his blood
questions.explanation: Verse 38 describes how dogs licked up Ahab's blood at the pool of Samaria, fulfilling the word of the LORD.

questions.question: What does 1 Kings 22 say about the record of King Ahab’s reign and deeds?
options: They are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel
They were inscribed on stone tablets
They were recorded by the prophets
questions.correctAnswer: They are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel
questions.explanation: Verse 39 states that the acts of Ahab are written in the chronicles of the kings of Israel.

questions.question: Who succeeded Ahab as king of Israel according to 1 Kings 22?
questions.correctAnswer: Ahaziah
questions.explanation: Verse 40 states that Ahaziah, Ahab’s son, reigned in his stead after Ahab died.

questions.question: How is Jehoshaphat’s reign described in terms of his age and length of reign in 1 Kings 22?
options: Began at 30 years old and reigned 20 years
Began at 35 years old and reigned 25 years
Began at 40 years old and reigned 15 years
Began at 25 years old and reigned 30 years
questions.correctAnswer: Began at 35 years old and reigned 25 years
questions.explanation: Verse 42 states Jehoshaphat was 35 years old when he began to reign and reigned 25 years in Jerusalem.

questions.question: True or False: Jehoshaphat completely removed the high places where people offered incense during his reign.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Verse 43 specifically says the high places were not taken away, and people still offered incense there.

questions.question: What significant diplomatic action did Jehoshaphat take towards Israel as described in 1 Kings 22?
questions.correctAnswer: He made peace
questions.explanation: Verse 44 states Jehoshaphat made peace with the king of Israel.

questions.question: What did Jehoshaphat do regarding the remnant of the sodomites during his reign according to 1 Kings 22?
options: He took them out of the land
questions.correctAnswer: He took them out of the land
questions.explanation: Verse 46 states Jehoshaphat removed the remnant of the sodomites remaining from his father’s days.

questions.question: What was the political situation in Edom during Jehoshaphat's reign as described in 1 Kings 22?
options: There was no king but a deputy ruled
questions.correctAnswer: There was no king but a deputy ruled
questions.explanation: Verse 47 notes that there was no king in Edom at that time, only a deputy as king.

questions.question: What happened to the ships Jehoshaphat made to go to Ophir for gold according to 1 Kings 22?
options: They were destroyed by a storm
questions.correctAnswer: They were broken at Eziongeber
questions.explanation: Verse 48 states the ships were broken at Eziongeber and did not go to Ophir.

questions.question: How did Jehoshaphat respond to Ahaziah's request to send servants with his servants on the ships?
questions.correctAnswer: He refused
questions.explanation: Verse 49 states Jehoshaphat would not allow Ahaziah’s servants to go with his servants on the ships.

questions.question: Who succeeded Jehoshaphat as king of Judah after his death as stated in 1 Kings 22?
questions.correctAnswer: Jehoram
questions.explanation: Verse 50 states Jehoshaphat was buried and Jehoram his son reigned in his stead.

questions.question: How long did Ahaziah son of Ahab reign over Israel according to 1 Kings 22?
questions.correctAnswer: Two years
questions.explanation: Verse 51 states Ahaziah reigned two years over Israel.

questions.question: True or False: Ahaziah walked in the ways of the LORD and did what was right during his reign.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Verse 52 states Ahaziah did evil in the sight of the LORD, walking in his parents' sinful ways.

questions.question: Which foreign god did Ahaziah serve and worship, provoking the LORD God of Israel according to 1 Kings 22?
questions.correctAnswer: Baal
questions.explanation: Verse 53 states Ahaziah served Baal and worshipped him, provoking the LORD.

theological.title: 1 Kings Chapter 22 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Kings Chapter 22 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What divine attribute is primarily demonstrated by the LORD's action of putting a lying spirit in the mouths of Ahab's prophets to bring about his downfall?
questions.correctAnswer: God's justice
questions.explanation: In 1 Kings 22:22-23, God allows a lying spirit to deceive Ahab's prophets, demonstrating His attribute of justice by executing judgment on Ahab for his sins.

questions.question: What does Micaiah's vision of Israel scattered like sheep without a shepherd symbolize the spiritual state of Israel at that time?
options: The nation is well-led and united
Israel is without effective leadership and vulnerable
The people are victorious in battle
questions.correctAnswer: Israel is without effective leadership and vulnerable
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 22:17 depicts Israel as sheep without a shepherd, symbolizing their lack of godly leadership and spiritual vulnerability, reflecting the consequences of their disobedience.

questions.question: According to 1 Kings 22, what does Jehoshaphat's insistence on enquiring of a prophet of the LORD indicate about his character and faith?
options: He is indifferent to God's guidance
He trusts in his own wisdom
He values divine revelation and guidance
questions.correctAnswer: He values divine revelation and guidance
questions.explanation: Jehoshaphat's request to seek a prophet of the LORD in 1 Kings 22:7-8 shows his desire to know God's will, demonstrating his faith and submission to divine authority.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is illustrated by the LORD’s sovereign control over spiritual beings deciding to send a lying spirit to deceive Ahab's prophets?
options: Doctrine of spiritual warfare and divine sovereignty
questions.correctAnswer: Doctrine of spiritual warfare and divine sovereignty
questions.explanation: Verses 20-23 show God's sovereign authority over heavenly hosts, including spirits, illustrating His control in spiritual warfare and His ultimate sovereignty over human events.

questions.question: How does the encounter between Zedekiah son of Chenaanah and Micaiah illustrate the conflict between true and false prophecy in Israel?
options: False prophets opposed and attacked true prophets
There was no distinction between true and false prophecy
questions.correctAnswer: False prophets opposed and attacked true prophets
questions.explanation: In 1 Kings 22:24, Zedekiah strikes Micaiah, showing the hostility false prophets had toward the true word of God, emphasizing the spiritual conflict between truth and deception.

questions.question: What does the death of King Ahab in battle and the subsequent actions with his body signify about God's judgment and prophecy fulfillment?
options: Ahab died peacefully and was honored
Ahab’s death and the dogs licking his blood fulfilled the prophecy of disgrace
Ahab escaped judgment by dying anonymously
questions.correctAnswer: Ahab’s death and the dogs licking his blood fulfilled the prophecy of disgrace
questions.explanation: Verses 34-38 describe Ahab’s death and the dogs licking his blood, fulfilling the prophecy of disgrace spoken by Elijah (1 Kings 21:19), demonstrating God's faithfulness in judgment.

questions.question: How does the alliance and joint military action of Jehoshaphat king of Judah with Ahab king of Israel reflect the redemptive narrative concerning Israel and Judah?
options: It shows complete unity under God's covenant
It reflects political alliances apart from God's ideal plan
It demonstrates perfect obedience to God
It marks the beginning of messianic prophecy
questions.correctAnswer: It reflects political alliances apart from God's ideal plan
questions.explanation: Jehoshaphat's alliance with Ahab (1 Kings 22:2, 29) reflects political pragmatism rather than covenant faithfulness, showing the flawed human attempts apart from God's ideal redemptive plan for unity.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God's sending of a lying spirit to deceive prophets contradicts His truthfulness. What does 1 Kings 22:20-23 actually teach about God's nature and purposes?
options: God is deceitful and changes His mind
God uses even deception to accomplish His just purposes
God is limited and powerless over spirits
God approves lying as a general principle
questions.correctAnswer: God uses even deception to accomplish His just purposes
questions.explanation: Verses 20-23 reveal God's sovereignty in permitting a lying spirit to fulfill His righteous judgment on Ahab, illustrating that God's ultimate purposes and justice override human understanding of truthfulness.

questions.question: What does Jehoshaphat’s refusal to let Ahaziah’s servants join his ships indicate about his spiritual discernment or leadership priorities?
options: He sought political alliance at any cost
He showed discernment in avoiding ungodly partnerships
He was indifferent to spiritual matters
He was trying to provoke war with Israel
questions.correctAnswer: He showed discernment in avoiding ungodly partnerships
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 22:49 describes Jehoshaphat refusing Ahaziah’s offer, which may indicate his spiritual discernment and caution in leadership to avoid ungodly influence.

questions.question: How do 1 Kings 22:42-43 demonstrate the doctrine of sanctification in Jehoshaphat’s reign despite the persistence of high places?
options: Jehoshaphat walked in righteousness but did not complete sanctification reforms
questions.correctAnswer: Jehoshaphat walked in righteousness but did not complete sanctification reforms
questions.explanation: Verses 42-43 show Jehoshaphat’s personal faithfulness, yet the high places remained, illustrating progressive sanctification where obedience increases but sin is not fully eradicated.

questions.question: What does the presence of a ‘deputy king’ in Edom during Jehoshaphat’s reign reveal about the political and spiritual state of neighboring nations in relation to Israel and Judah’s covenant faithfulness?
options: Edom was fully independent and godly
Edom lacked a true king indicating political instability
Edom was a model of covenant faithfulness
Edom was united under one strong king
questions.correctAnswer: Edom lacked a true king indicating political instability
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 22:47 notes there was no king in Edom, only a deputy, suggesting political instability possibly reflecting consequences of idolatry and covenant unfaithfulness in surrounding nations.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight about divine sovereignty and human responsibility is conveyed by comparing 1 Kings 22:16 and 1 Kings 22:34-35?
options: Human actions are irrelevant to divine plans
God’s sovereign will works through human decisions and consequences
God’s plans are unpredictable and arbitrary
questions.correctAnswer: God’s sovereign will works through human decisions and consequences
questions.explanation: Verse 16 shows the king demanding truth, affirming human responsibility, while verses 34-35 show Ahab’s death as consequence and divine will, combining to teach that God’s sovereignty includes human accountability.

questions.question: How does the prophecy of Ahab’s defeat at Ramothgilead and the subsequent fulfillment illustrate the reliability of God’s word and prophetic ministry?
options: God’s word through prophecy is trustworthy and fulfilled
Prophets often contradict each other without consequence
Prophecy is symbolic and never fulfilled literally
questions.correctAnswer: God’s word through prophecy is trustworthy and fulfilled
questions.explanation: The narrative from verses 15, 29-37 shows the prophecy concerning Ahab’s death at Ramothgilead fulfilled exactly, affirming the trustworthiness of God’s prophetic word.

questions.question: What does Jehoshaphat’s reign, described in 1 Kings 22:41-44, reveal about the possibility of imperfect holiness and grace within God’s covenant people?
options: God’s people must be perfect or face rejection
God’s covenant allows for growth despite imperfections
Sin is not tolerated in any measure
Holiness is irrelevant in covenant life
questions.correctAnswer: God’s covenant allows for growth despite imperfections
questions.explanation: Verses 41-44 describe Jehoshaphat’s generally faithful reign despite remaining high places, illustrating that covenant relationship includes grace and progressive sanctification.

questions.question: What do the contrasting prophecies of the 400 prophets and Micaiah teach about discerning true prophecy and divine truth?
options: Majority opinion always reflects God’s truth
True prophecy may often be unpopular and opposed
All prophets spoke the same message
questions.correctAnswer: True prophecy may often be unpopular and opposed
questions.explanation: Verses 6-8 and 14-17 show 400 prophets predicting victory, but Micaiah’s true prophecy foretells defeat, teaching that true prophecy may be opposed and unpopular yet aligned with God’s truth.
